analysis: This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the date (line 3) and adds documentation at head lines 1293-1298 for `PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup`. The lookup now snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations, so a promotion that rotates the cache cannot turn a later piece in the same lookup into a miss. The doc says token arrays share storage during the snapshot, existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. No code, wire contract, key handling, attestation or authorization changes appear in the supplied evidence. Security relevance is limited to T-041 (prefix-cache and TTFT oracle) and the prompt-token cache (`PromptTokenCache`). The doc states reuse never crosses a cache scope and the bounds are unchanged, so the documented behavior does not widen the cross-tenant timing channel (SEC-035) or at-rest exposure. The prompt-token cache is in-memory, not the SSD tier. Not verified: the underlying Swift change in PromptTokenCache.swift is not supplied. A deeper pass should confirm that the snapshot's shared storage is scope-keyed, bounds still hold, and the lookup does not introduce a new hit/miss timing difference beyond what T-041 already accepts. The rest of the document is unchanged context and I raised no pre-existing issues. The documentation claims are not verifiable against code here, so I record that as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
